title.narrative: PPDP Volvo/UNIDO Ungdomssysselsättning inom HDEICV i DRC
PPDP Volvo/UNIDO youth employment in HDIECV in DRC

description.narrative:
Projektet är ett så kallat Public Private Development Partnership (PPDP), som genomförs av FN:s industriutvecklingsorganisation (UNIDO) i samarbete med företagen Volvo och Epiroc. Syftet är att bidra till ungdomssysselsättning inom tung industriutrustning och kommersiella fordon (HDIECV) i två av de 26 provinserna i Demokratiska republiken Kongo (DRK). Ett centralt inslag i projektet är att främja kompetensutveckling för unga män och kvinnor genom teknisk utbildning och yrkesutbildning (TVET), kompletterad med stödjande insatser, för att därigenom stärka både utbud och efterfrågan på ungdomsarbetskraft på HDIECV-marknaden.
Projektet har en systemförändrande ansats genom att bidra med en ny sorts yrkesutbildning där privata aktörer är involverade från början och bidrar med egna resurser. Medverkan från kongolesiska myndigheter ska göra att modellen blir känd, etablerad och även kan användas i andra sektorer.
Projektet är planerat för en period på 5 år, från april 2022 till mars 2027, vilket betyder att projektet kommer att fortsätta bortom slutdatumet för den nuvarande svenska regeringens strategi för DRK.

The project is a Public Private Development Partnership (PPDP), implemented by the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) in collaboration with the Volvo Group (Volvo) and Epiroc, to generate youth employment in the Heavy Duty Industrial Equipment and Commercial Vehicle (HDIECV) sector in two out of the 26 provinces in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). A key focus of the project is to promote skills development for young men and women through Technical and Vocational Training (TVET), complemented with related interventions, to thereby strengthen both supply and demand for youth labour in the HDIECV market.
The project aims for systemic change by showing a new model for vocational training where private actors are involved from the start and also contribute with their own resources. Participation from Congolese authorities will make the model known and established so that it can also be used in other sectors.
The project is planned for a period of 5 years, from April 2022 until March 2027, which is beyond the current Swedish government strategy for DRC.

The intervention is a Public Private Partnership Development Partnership (PPDP) initiative, implemented by UNIDO in collaboration with Swedish companies Volvo and Epiroc to generate jobs for young people in the heavy industrial equipment and construction sector. utility vehicles (HDIECV) in two (Lualaba and Haut Katanga) provinces out of the 26 in the DRC.
The project aims to promote the development of technical skills among young Congolese men and women (mainly those between the ages of 15 and 35). This will enhance the youth workforce in the HDIECV market.

In this third year, the Project has made remarkable progress in collaboration between stakeholders, program modernization, and the establishment of the ITIMA and INPP Centers of Excellence (CE). The project has maintained ongoing dialogue with all partners and stakeholders. Relations between partners are good. This is one of the projects that has received numerous visits, not only by the program officer, but also during joint monitoring and ad hoc visits during various events in the intervention areas. For example, the Nkelo Bantu Conference in Kolwezi in March 2024 and Mining Week in June 2025 in Lubumbashi. This has allowed Sweden to maintain dialogue and support the project in addressing the challenges facing the partner. For example, advocacy with the authorities regarding fundraising issues for both INPP and ITIMA beneficiaries. The Ambassador personally intervened on behalf of INPP and ITIMA. In addition to the monitoring missions, Sweden organized several online follow-up meetings with UNIDO and all Swedish partner companies to ensure the project's progress, including the thorny issue of the construction/rehabilitation of centers of excellence, which was experiencing funding difficulties.
The project also held its annual steering committee meeting, which brought together all stakeholders, including ministries, direct beneficiaries of the INPP-ITIMA project, and the Swedish companies SMT/Volvo and Epiroc, to review project progress and validate the narrative reports, annual financial reports, and the 2024-2025 activity schedule.
For Sweden, this intervention is gradually impacting the Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) environment in four areas: the modernization/construction of a TVET facility with well-equipped workshops; skills development/training of TVET teachers; involvement of the private sector in planning and support for simulation equipment for workshops; as well as the effective start of training for young people and employees in the maintenance of heavy machinery and utility vehicles.
The modernization/construction of a TVET facility with well-equipped workshops:
For the INPP Center of Excellence, the construction of the workshop is currently in its final phase, to everyone's great satisfaction. This workshop is funded by the INPP's own funds to the tune of approximately USD 787,000.00. Some finishing work still remains to be done, particularly regarding the electrical and painting work. The financing of the workshop's construction by the INPP General Directorate demonstrates a strong political will to implement technical and vocational training programs.
In contrast, for ITIMA, the second beneficiary of the project struggled to secure state funds for the rehabilitation of its workshop, which was intended to train young people as a center of excellence. However, thanks to additional funding from ENABEL (Belgian Cooperation), as part of its project to support the Lualaba Resource Center, construction work on this center did not begin until August 2025, with the development of the site. Fortunately, in collaboration with ENABEL, the construction schedule was revised to prioritize the construction of the workshop, ensuring its operationality as soon as possible, by January 2026. This construction work should receive close attention, as the availability of the workshop is a condition for obtaining the experimental order for ELVC maintenance programs in the national education sector. It is up to PAFEQ to capitalize on the entire construction implementation process and report evidence of the construction progress to MINEDUC in order to obtain the green light for the course experiment and allow students to enroll in the program.
Private sector involvement in planning and providing simulation equipment support for the workshops:
Through monitoring missions to verify the project's progress and ongoing dialogue with all stakeholders, a significant alignment was noted between these two aspects, contrary to initial assumptions. The growing involvement of private partner companies in the projectthrough their participation, contributions, and involvement in trainingtestifies to an effective synergy of the actions of all participants. This dynamic largely favored the launch, in April 2025, of the first professional training sessions for company employees, provided by the INPP. To date, two major companies have formally submitted their requests for continuing education for their employees: SEP-CONGO and MULYKAP. These requests were handled by the PAFEQ project in collaboration with the INPP. As the workshops are not yet ready, UNIDO has adopted the alternative of organizing the training sessions on company premises. It is now possible that other mining companies may be willing to donate equipment, which initially seemed unlikely.
In addition to the construction of the INPP workshop, it is worth noting that the equipment provided by private contributors SMT, Volvo, and EPIROC is already on site in Lubumbashi, which is a very positive development. Sweden is increasingly noting that UNIDO has launched several parallel initiatives to try to make up for the delays already incurred. This is so that, once the centers of excellence are completed, everything will be in place for the start of technical training for the young beneficiaries. It is also worth noting that two containers valued at USD 1,465,033 were provided by Volvo, the main donor, along with a consignment worth USD 140,000 from SMT and a set of equipment valued at approximately USD 61,000 from EPIROC.
Skills development/training of TVET teachers : Programs and guides to standardize and improve vocational training have been developed in accordance with national standards governing the two partner pilot training centers. During this year, more than ten (10) general support guides; three (3) pedagogical guides, including two (2) for INPP (assistant mechanic and maintenance mechanic for heavy equipment and commercial vehicles) and one (1) for ITIMA (secondary level); three (3) training reference guides, including two for INPP and one for ITIMA; and finally, a reference guide for skills assessment and certification for ITIMA, have been produced.
Ten (10) printed modules with illustrations, including six for road vehicles and four for construction equipment; fifteen (15) electronic modules with illustrations, including eleven for construction equipment and four for road vehicles, were finalized in April 2025. These modules will be made available to the two partner training centers (INPP and ITIMA) for course design and preparation.
Two workshops were organized in Kinshasa in October 2024 to gather national feedback on the training program development process. 32 participants took part, including 16 from INPP, 15 from MINEDUC-NC, and 1 from the national FEC. A workshop to validate the training standards and the pedagogical guide was held in Lubumbashi in July 2024, with 22 participants, including the national delegation of MINEDUC-NC and the general management of INPP, as well as other partners, notably SMT/Volvo, EPIROC, Enabel, and the FEC Haut Katanga. Support for the management and improvement of training quality.
In conclusion, the project is progressing promisingly. However, a disparity persists between the two provinces. The INPP center of excellence in Lubumbashi is nearing completion, while construction of the ITIMA center in Kolwezi began last August.
